Consult Summary:
- Female patient with 2 days of central lower abdominal pain, subjective fever/diaphoresis, nausea, and reported slight hematuria; clinician suspected urinary tract infection and recommended a short course of antibiotics with safety-netting.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Lower abdominal (lower tummy) pain for 2 days; described as central.
  - Feeling hot and sweaty; measured temperature ~37.0°C one hour prior to consult.
  - Mild nausea without vomiting.
  - Reported slight pink discoloration of urine ("some... a little bit pink").
  - No back pain, no pelvic/vaginal discharge, no abnormal vaginal bleeding.
- Timeline:
  - Pain onset: 2 days ago.
  - Constipation occurred during the prior week but bowel habit reportedly normal now; last bowel movement approximately 2 hours before consult and described as normal.
  - Temperature measured ~37.0°C one hour before consult; no other documented elevated readings.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - None specifically identified.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - Urination: slight increase in frequency; no pain on passing urine reported; no strong smell to urine.
  - Thirst: reports increased thirst.
  - No vomiting, no acid reflux symptoms, no shivering beyond feeling sweaty.
  - No recent travel.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No prior similar episodes.
  - No back pain (no flank pain).
  - No vaginal discharge, no intermenstrual or postcoital bleeding.
  - No recent other medical problems apart from routine minor illnesses (cold/flu).

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported; patient states "nothing sore" aside from usual colds/flus.
- Gynecologic: had an internal contraceptive implant for one year previously; patient states "now no more" (timing/details not documented).
- Allergies:
  - Amoxicillin.
- Medications:
  - No regular medications reported.
  - No over-the-counter medications reported.

Social History:
- Lives with parents.
- Tobacco: does not smoke.
- Alcohol: drinks approximately 4 times per week, about one beer per occasion.
- Substance use: not reported.
- Occupational/financial details: not reported.

Family History:
- Mother had breast cancer; reportedly cured. No other family history detailed.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals:
  - Temperature ~37.0°C (measured by patient one hour prior to consult).
- Examination findings:
  - No clinician-performed physical examination findings documented.

Investigations:
- No investigations or tests documented (no urine dipstick, culture, pregnancy test, blood tests, or imaging performed/documented).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected urinary tract infection (as per clinician)
  - Assessment:
    - Clinical impression: possible UTI given lower abdominal pain, increased urinary frequency, and reported pink urine; low-grade temperature and nausea present.
  - Plan items:
    - Offer of antibiotic treatment: clinician recommended a 3-day course of antibiotics, to be taken twice daily.
      - Medication name not documented; dose/route not documented. (Frequency and duration documented: twice daily for 3 days.)
    - Prescription to be sent to patient's allocated Babylon pharmacy if patient agrees.
    - Start antibiotics as soon as obtained.
    - Safety-netting: advise patient to re-contact immediately or arrange face-to-face assessment if:
      - Pain worsens,
      - High temperature develops,
      - Back pain or new/worsening symptoms occur,
      - Symptoms do not improve or recur — face-to-face examination may then be required.
- Issue 2: None further documented.
- Issue 3: None further documented.
- General plan items:
  - No additional investigations or follow-up appointments documented beyond advice to re-contact if worsening or non-resolution.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No urine dipstick, urine microscopy/culture, or pregnancy test documented.
  - No clinician-recorded vital signs other than the patient's single temperature measurement.
  - No physical examination findings (abdominal, pelvic, or flank exam) documented.
  - No specific antibiotic name, dose, or route documented (only frequency and duration provided).
  - Limited sexual history and STI risk assessment not documented.
  - Contraceptive implant details (dates, removal status) unclear.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - None major; patient reports feeling hot/sweaty yet measured temperature ~37.0°C; both statements recorded (no direct contradiction).
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally intelligible; occasional pauses, filler words, and minor unclear phrasing. No major portions inaudible.
